ai_summary: Great Britain's wind generation currently stands at 2.6 GW, with Scottish wind contributing an estimated 1.6 GW, representing 15.8% of installed Scottish wind capacity. This localized clean generation allows Scotland to record a carbon intensity of 0 gCO2/kWh, contrasting sharply with the GB-wide carbon intensity of 172 gCO2/kWh. However, transmission bottlenecks across the boundary continue to restrict export flows, resulting in 490 MWh of Scottish generation curtailed so far today through Balancing Mechanism bids. Managing these network constraints has incurred a direct cost of about £30,168. Annualizing this rate yields an estimated yearly curtailment cost of approximately £11 million, which adds an estimated £0.04/MWh to electricity invoices across the UK. Beyond the direct financial impact, displacing this zero-carbon generation requires fossil-fueled replacement plant elsewhere on the network. An estimated 93,100 m³ of gas was burned elsewhere to replace the turned-down wind power, releasing 172 tonnes of additional CO2 into the atmosphere. This operational imbalance underscores the ongoing environmental and system balancing costs of grid congestion during periods of regional curtailment.
